Prevention: Use proper phytosanitary measures and clean palm crown at regular intervals.
Remove and burn fallen, immature, mite-infested nuts.
Provide adequate irrigation during summer months.
Conserve soil moisture at the base of the tree by mulching with coconut husk/water hyacinth/ paddy straw.
Use recommended nitrogen and phosphorus nutrients from
Apply nutrients in 2 equal splits (before rainy season and after rainy season).
Monitoring: Carefully observe fallen nuts during the months of
May for symptoms of eriophyid mite damage.
The mites are too small to be seen.
The damage appears as triangular yellowish brown patches extending distally on the fruit surface from beneath the perianth.
As the age of the nuts increases this damage spreads out from beneath the perianth.
Damaged surfaces dry up and build up longitudinally.

Direct Control: Remove affected young fruits and destroy by burning.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Spray crown adjacent to the branch region with 1.5-2.0% Omite (miticide) after removing infected nuts.
Spray only pollinated bunches; avoid spraying leaves.
Spray nearby young and healthy plants with 1.5-2.0% Propargite (miticide).
